original_question: Is it true that for every point [Gamma] in Hilb_d(A^3), the parity of d matches the parity of the dimension of the tangent space at [Gamma]?
target_in_paper: Section 2.6, (Solved) Problem XXV: the parity question for tangent-space dimensions on Hilb^d(A^3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content almost verbatim: it asks about points of the Hilbert scheme of d points in affine 3-space and compares the parity of d with the parity of the tangent-space dimension at that point. This is exactly the issue raised in Problem XXV, up to the paper-wide notation and conventions supplied earlier in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
missing_details: The paper-wide convention is that everything is over an algebraically closed field k, so the ambient space should be written as A^3_k rather than an unspecified A^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
The outer quantifier over the degree should be explicit: the question is for every positive integer d and every point [Gamma] in Hilb^d(A^3_k). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

To be fully stand-alone, [Gamma] should be identified with a zero-dimensional subscheme Gamma subset A^3_k of length d, since Hilb^d(X) parametrizes finite degree-d subschemes of X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

The tangent space should be named explicitly as the Zariski tangent space T_[Gamma]Hilb^d(A^3_k), and the parity claim should be written as a congruence modulo 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
Paper-faithful notation is Hilb^d(A^3_k) rather than Hilb_d(A^3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

No homogeneity, monomial, grading, characteristic-zero, nilpotency, variable-by-variable, degree restriction, or sufficiently-large-m hypothesis belongs in the statement itself; the surrounding text mentions monomial and graded cases only as known affirmative special cases, not as assumptions of the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field, let d > 0, and let [Gamma] in Hilb^d(A^3_k) be the point corresponding to a zero-dimensional subscheme Gamma subset A^3_k of length d. Is it true that the Zariski tangent-space dimension at [Gamma] has the same parity as d; equivalently, that dim_k T_[Gamma]Hilb^d(A^3_k) is congruent to d modulo 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2.6, (Solved) Problem XXV, whose official formulation is this global parity question for arbitrary points of Hilb^d(A^3). Section 1.3 supplies the hidden conventions needed to make it stand-alone: the base field k is algebraically closed and Hilb^d(X) denotes the Hilbert scheme of finite degree-d subschemes of X. The nearby context after Problem XXV shows that one should not weaken or alter the target to the dense-open version, nor add a grading assumption: monomial and graded ideals are mentioned only as partial affirmative cases, and the weaker dense-open question is explicitly stated separately. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
